source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Unit 9 (PDF 256-275), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh Unit 9 (Inverse Trigonometric (TOC: 'Inverse Trigonometric Functions and Their Graphs')) ke poore unit se practice MCQs hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah, jis mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.
9.1 Inverse Trigonometric Functions and their Graph

blocks.prompt:
1 Which kind of function has an inverse function?
(Kis qism ke function ka inverse function hota hai?)

options.text: jo function one-to-one aur onto (bijective) ho

blocks.explanation: Sirf one-to-one aur onto (bijective) function ka inverse hota hai: har output sirf aik input se aaye aur codomain ka har element output ho.

book_ref.quote: only a one-to-one and onto function will have an inverse

blocks.prompt:
2 If \(f : X \to Y\) is bijective, then the range of \(f^{-1}\) is:
(Agar \(f : X \to Y\) bijective ho to \(f^{-1}\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inverse \(Y\) se wapas \(X\) ki taraf jata hai: \(f^{-1}\) ki domain = \(f\) ki range, aur \(f^{-1}\) ki range = \(f\) ki domain \(= X\).

book_ref.quote: is a bijective function from the set \(Y\) back to the set \(X\)

blocks.prompt:
3 The trigonometric functions are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\) mainly because they are:
(Trigonometric functions \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one kyun nahin hote? Kyunke woh:)
blocks.explanation: Yeh periodic (dohrane wale) hain: apni values baar baar dohrate hain, is liye bohat se angles aik hi value dete hain aur function one-to-one nahin rehta.

book_ref.quote: Due to this periodicity, trigonometric functions are generally not bijective

blocks.prompt:
4 The statement \(\frac{\pi}{3} = \sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) means the same as:
(Bayan \(\frac{\pi}{3} = \sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ka matlab kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \sin y\). Yahan \(y = \frac{\pi}{3}\), \(x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\): yaani \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: This means \(y\) is an angle whose sine is \(x\)

blocks.prompt:
5 Another name for \(\sin^{-1} x\) is:
(\(\sin^{-1} x\) ka doosra naam kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin^{-1} x\) ko 'sine inverse of \(x\)' ya 'arcsine of \(x\)' parhte hain, yaani \(\arcsin x\). Baqi teenon reciprocal \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) hain.

blocks.prompt:
6 The one angle given by an inverse trigonometric function (from its restricted interval) is called the:
(Inverse trigonometric function jo aik angle deta hai (restricted interval se), use kya kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Domain ko aik standard interval tak mehdood karne se sirf aik angle bachta hai; usay principal value (asal qeemat) kehte hain.

book_ref.quote: The single angle chosen in this way is called the principal value.

blocks.prompt:
7 \(f(x) = x^{2}\) is not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\). On which set is it one-to-one?
(\(f(x) = x^{2}\) \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one nahin. Kis set par one-to-one hai?)
blocks.explanation: \([0, \infty)\) par mukhtalif inputs ke squares mukhtalif hain. Baqi sets mein \(-1, 1\) jaise jore hain jin ka square aik hi \(1\) hai.

book_ref.quote: If a function is not one-to-one, it may be possible to restrict its domain to make it one-to-one

blocks.prompt:
8 The domain of the principal sine function is:
(Principal sine function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sine ko band interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) tak mehdood karte hain; wahan yeh \(-1\) se \(1\) tak barhta hai aur har value aik dafa leta hai.

book_ref.quote: is called the principal sine function

blocks.prompt:
9 The domain of \(\sin^{-1} x\) is:
(\(\sin^{-1} x\) ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inverse ki domain principal sine ki range hoti hai, yaani \([-1, 1]\).

book_ref.quote: where the domain of \(\sin^{-1} x\) is \([-1, 1]\)

blocks.prompt:
10 The principal value of \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) is:
(\(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) ki principal value kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) aur sine odd hai, is liye \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) range mein hai. \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hain.

book_ref.quote: This is the test for every answer

blocks.prompt:
11 \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\) equals:
(\(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Manfi input ka jawab manfi angle: \(\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) aur \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) range mein hai.

book_ref.quote: are covered by the negative angles

blocks.prompt:
12 \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\) equals:
(\(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), aur \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3}\). \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hai, is liye jawab nahin.

book_ref.quote: must lie between \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)

blocks.prompt:
13 Which one of the following does NOT exist?
(In mein se kaun si qeemat mojood NAHIN?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka input \([-1, 1]\) mein hona chahiye, aur \(\frac{3}{2} > 1\). Baqi sab defined hain (\(\tan^{-1}\) har real number leta hai).

book_ref.quote: does not exist, because no angle has sine 2

blocks.prompt:
14 The reciprocal \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) is equal to:
(Reciprocal \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\). \(\sin^{-1} x\) mein \(-1\) inverse function ka naam hai, power nahin.

book_ref.quote: a completely different function

blocks.prompt:
15 The graph of \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) is the mirror image of the principal sine graph in the line:
(\(y = \sin^{-1} x\) ka graph principal sine graph ka kis line mein aks (mirror image) hai?)
blocks.explanation: \((a, b)\) ka \(y = x\) mein aks \((b, a)\) hai; function aur us ke inverse ka yehi rishta hai.

book_ref.quote: So the graph of any inverse function is the reflection of the graph of the function

blocks.prompt:
16 The point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) lies on the principal sine graph. The matching point on \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) is:
(Point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) principal sine graph par hai. \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) par mutabiq point kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Coordinates jagah badalte hain: \((a, b) \to (b, a)\), is liye \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\).

book_ref.quote: Every point \((a, b)\) of \(y = \sin x\) gives the point \((b, a)\) of \(y = \sin^{-1} x\)

blocks.prompt:
17 Besides the principal interval, sine is also one-to-one on:
(Principal interval ke ilawa sine kis interval par bhi one-to-one hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\) par (\(n = 1\)) sine \(1\) se \(-1\) tak musalsal ghatta hai. \([0, \pi]\) par \(\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \sin\frac{5\pi}{6}\); \(\left[\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{5\pi}{4}\right]\) par \(\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\).

book_ref.quote: where it is strictly increasing or decreasing, to make the sine function one-to-one

blocks.prompt:
18 \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) equals:
(\(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\), aur \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\) ki principal value \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) hai.

book_ref.quote: If the interval is not specified, then

blocks.prompt:
19 The domain of the principal cosine function is:
(Principal cosine function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Band interval \([0, \pi]\) par cosine \(1\) se \(-1\) tak ghatta hai aur har value aik dafa leta hai.

book_ref.quote: is called the principal cosine function

blocks.prompt:
20 \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) equals:
(\(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) range \([0, \pi]\) mein hai.

book_ref.quote: The domain of \(\cos^{-1} x\) is \([-1, 1]\) and the range of \(\cos^{-1} x\) is \([0, \pi]\).

blocks.prompt:
21 \(\cos^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) equals:
(\(\cos^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) range mein hai. (\(\frac{\pi}{3}\) to \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hai.)

book_ref.quote: Some values of the principal inverse cosine

blocks.prompt:
22 For \(-1 \le x \le 1\), \(\cos^{-1}(-x)\) is equal to:
(\(-1 \le x \le 1\) ke liye \(\cos^{-1}(-x)\) kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: Kyunke \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\) aur \(\pi - \cos^{-1} x\) range \([0, \pi]\) mein rehta hai. (\(-\cos^{-1} x\) sine wala qaida hai.)

book_ref.quote: A pattern you can see in the table

blocks.prompt:
23 \(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\) equals:
(\(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\); \([0, \pi]\) mein cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\) wala angle \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.

book_ref.quote: Look at the negative inputs in the table: they give obtuse angles.

blocks.prompt:
24 Why is cosine NOT restricted to \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) to define \(\cos^{-1}\)?
(\(\cos^{-1}\) ke liye cosine ko \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) tak mehdood kyun NAHIN karte?)

options.text: cosine even hai, is liye wahan one-to-one nahin

blocks.explanation: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\), maslan \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{4}\): do inputs aik output. Wahan cosine manfi bhi nahin hota.

book_ref.quote: Cosine is an even function, so a negative angle and the matching positive angle always give the same value.

blocks.prompt:
25 As \(x\) increases from \(-1\) to \(1\), \(\cos^{-1} x\):
(Jab \(x\) \(-1\) se \(1\) tak barhta hai to \(\cos^{-1} x\):)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos^{-1}(-1) = \pi\) aur \(\cos^{-1} 1 = 0\); graph \((-1, \pi)\) se \((1, 0)\) tak neeche aata hai.

book_ref.quote: A larger number has a smaller angle.

blocks.prompt:
26 Besides \([0, \pi]\), cosine is also one-to-one on:
(\([0, \pi]\) ke ilawa cosine kis interval par bhi one-to-one hai?)
blocks.explanation: \([\pi, 2\pi]\) yaani \(n = 1\); wahan cosine \(-1\) se \(1\) tak barhta hai. Baqi intervals mein \(\pm\frac{\pi}{4}\) ya \(\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{4}\) jaise jore aik hi cosine dete hain.

book_ref.quote: or generally \([n\pi, n\pi + \pi]\)

blocks.prompt:
27 Which one of the following can NOT be a value of \(\cos^{-1} x\)?
(In mein se kaun si \(\cos^{-1} x\) ki value NAHIN ho sakti?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos^{-1}\) ki range \([0, \pi]\) hai; manfi angle kabhi value nahin hota.

book_ref.quote: of a negative number is an obtuse angle in

blocks.prompt:
28 \(\tan x\) is NOT defined at:
(\(\tan x\) kahan defined NAHIN?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) aur \(\cos x = 0\) theek \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke odd multiples par hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Division by zero is not defined, so these points are not in the domain.

blocks.prompt:
29 The domain of the principal tangent function is:
(Principal tangent function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh khula (open) interval hai: \(\tan\left(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) undefined hai, is liye end points shamil nahin.

book_ref.quote: is called the principal tangent function

blocks.prompt:
30 The domain of \(\tan^{-1} x\) is:
(\(\tan^{-1} x\) ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Principal tangent har real value leta hai, is liye us ka inverse har real number qabool karta hai.

book_ref.quote: The domain of \(\tan^{-1} x\) is \((-\infty, \infty)\)

blocks.prompt:
31 The principal value of \(\tan^{-1}(-1)\) is:
(\(\tan^{-1}(-1)\) ki principal value kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\) aur tangent odd hai; manfi value ka jawab manfi angle \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\).

book_ref.quote: Use the sign and the principal range to place the angle

blocks.prompt:
32 \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\) equals:
(\(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) range mein hai. \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\), \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hain.

book_ref.quote: Find the reference angle from the standard values, ignoring the sign.

blocks.prompt:
33 The asymptotes of the graph of \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) are:
(\(y = \tan^{-1} x\) ke graph ke asymptotes kaun se hain?)
blocks.explanation: Principal tangent ke vertical asymptotes \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(y = x\) mein aks ke baad horizontal \(y = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) ban jate hain.

book_ref.quote: the coordinates swap, so vertical lines turn into horizontal lines

blocks.prompt:
34 \(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\) equals:
(\(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\frac{4\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}\), aur \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}\) (principal branch ka angle).

book_ref.quote: Each of these intervals is one complete branch of Figure 9.7

blocks.prompt:
35 The equation \(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) has:
(Equation (muadla) \(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) ke kitne hal hain?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan^{-1}\) ki range khula interval \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) hai; \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) kabhi nahin milta.

book_ref.quote: Why an open interval this time (round brackets)?

blocks.prompt:
36 Which inverse function accepts every real number as its input?
(Kaun sa inverse function har real number ko input ke tor par leta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan^{-1}\) ki domain \(\mathbb{R}\) hai; \(\sin^{-1}\), \(\cos^{-1}\) ko \([-1, 1]\) aur \(\sec^{-1}\) ko \(|x| \ge 1\) chahiye.

book_ref.quote: taking every real value exactly once: one-to-one and onto

blocks.prompt:
37 The domain of \(\csc x\) is \(\mathbb{R}\) without the points:
(\(\csc x\) ki domain \(\mathbb{R}\) mein se kaun se points nikaal kar hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\), aur \(\sin x = 0\) jab \(x = n\pi\).

book_ref.quote: Division by zero is not allowed, so we remove every \(x\) where

blocks.prompt:
38 The range of \(\csc x\) is:
(\(\csc x\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(|\sin x| \le 1\) se \(|\csc x| \ge 1\), yaani \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: the reciprocal always has size at least 1

blocks.prompt:
39 The domain of the principal cosecant function is:
(Principal cosecant function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh sine wala interval hai jis mein se \(0\) nikaal diya, kyunke \(\sin 0 = 0\).

book_ref.quote: called principal cosecant function

blocks.prompt:
40 \(\csc^{-1}\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) equals:
(\(\csc^{-1}\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc y = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) yaani \(\sin y = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), is liye \(y = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: A quick example of our own. Find

blocks.explanation: \(\sin y = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(y\) principal range mein: \(y = -\frac{\pi}{6}\).

book_ref.quote: Giving an answer outside \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)

blocks.prompt:
42 Which value is never taken by \(\csc^{-1} x\)?
(\(\csc^{-1} x\) kaun si value kabhi nahin leta?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc 0\) undefined hai, is liye \(0\) range mein nahin.

book_ref.quote: That is why 0 is not in the range.

blocks.prompt:
43 For which value of \(x\) is \(\csc^{-1} x\) NOT defined?
(\(x\) ki kis value ke liye \(\csc^{-1} x\) defined NAHIN?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc^{-1}\) ki domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\) hai; \(\frac{1}{3}\) is ke beech mein hai.

book_ref.quote: never takes a value strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\)

blocks.prompt:
44 The domain of the principal secant function is:
(Principal secant function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh cosine wala interval \([0, \pi]\) hai jis mein se \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) nikaal diya, kyunke \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\).

book_ref.quote: is called principal secant function

blocks.prompt:
45 \(\sec^{-1}(-\sqrt{2})\) equals:
(\(\sec^{-1}(-\sqrt{2})\) kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: negative angles are outside the range of

blocks.prompt:
46 \(\sec^{-1}\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) equals:
(\(\sec^{-1}\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos y = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(y \in [0, \pi]\): \(y = \frac{5\pi}{6}\). \(\sec^{-1}\) ka jawab kabhi manfi nahin.

book_ref.quote: Giving a negative answer for

blocks.prompt:
47 Which value is never taken by \(\sec^{-1} x\)?
(\(\sec^{-1} x\) kaun si value kabhi nahin leta?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sec\frac{\pi}{2}\) undefined hai, is liye \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) range mein nahin.

book_ref.quote: Including \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) in the range

blocks.prompt:
48 The horizontal asymptote of the graph of \(y = \sec^{-1} x\) is:
(\(y = \sec^{-1} x\) ke graph ka horizontal asymptote kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Principal secant ka vertical asymptote \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), aks ke baad \(y = \frac{\pi}{2}\) ban jata hai.

book_ref.quote: comes as close as we like to

blocks.prompt:
49 For \(x \ge 1\), the value of \(\sec^{-1} x\) lies in:
(\(x \ge 1\) ke liye \(\sec^{-1} x\) ki value kis interval mein hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x \ge 1\) ho to \(\cos y = \frac{1}{x}\) musbat, is liye \(y \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

book_ref.quote: For \(x \ge 1\) the values lie in

blocks.prompt:
50 The domain of the principal cotangent function is:
(Principal cotangent function ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cot x\) \(0\) aur \(\pi\) par undefined hai; \((0, \pi)\) par har real value aik dafa leta hai.

book_ref.quote: called principal cotangent function

blocks.prompt:
51 \(\cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) equals:
(\(\cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cot\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\); manfi value ke liye angle \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) mein: \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: become the horizontal asymptotes

blocks.prompt:
52 The range of \(\cot x\) is:
(\(\cot x\) ki range kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Har branch par \(\cot x\) \(+\infty\) se \(-\infty\) tak jata hai, is liye har real number value hai.

book_ref.quote: Unlike \(\csc x\) and \(\sec x\), \(\cot x\) takes every real value

blocks.prompt:
53 \(\cot^{-1} 0\) equals:
(\(\cot^{-1} 0\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\cot\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2} \in (0, \pi)\).

book_ref.quote: there is one complete branch

blocks.prompt:
54 \(\tan\left[\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\) equals:
(\(\tan\left[\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: Andar wala angle: \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\). Phir \(\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

book_ref.quote: Method: work from the inside out.

blocks.prompt:
55 \(\sec\left[\cot^{-1}(-1)\right]\) equals:
(\(\sec\left[\cot^{-1}(-1)\right]\) kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: First find the inner angle

blocks.prompt:
56 For every inverse trigonometric function, its domain is:
(Har inverse trigonometric function ki domain kya hoti hai?)

options.text: us ke principal function ki range
us ke principal function ki domain

blocks.explanation: Domain aur range jagah badalte hain: inverse ki domain principal function ki range hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: each inverse function's domain is the range of its principal function

blocks.prompt:
57 The domain of \(f(x) = \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)\) is:
(\(f(x) = \sin^{-1}(2x + 1)\) ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(-1 \le 2x + 1 \le 1 \Rightarrow -1 \le x \le 0\).

book_ref.quote: an inverse trigonometric function only accepts inputs from its own domain

blocks.prompt:
58 The domain of \(g(x) = \sec^{-1}(2x)\) is:
(\(g(x) = \sec^{-1}(2x)\) ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(2x \le -1\) ya \(2x \ge 1\), yaani \(x \le -\frac{1}{2}\) ya \(x \ge \frac{1}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: \(\sec^{-1}\) needs the input in \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)

blocks.prompt:
59 The domain of \(h(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(e^{x}\right)\) is:
(\(h(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(e^{x}\right)\) ki domain kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(-1 \le e^{x} \le 1\) chahiye. \(e^{x}\) hamesha musbat hai, is liye sirf \(e^{x} \le 1\): \(x \le 0\).

book_ref.quote: remember any extra condition such as

blocks.prompt:
60 For \(|x| \ge 1\), \(\csc^{-1} x\) is equal to:
(\(|x| \ge 1\) ke liye \(\csc^{-1} x\) kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc y = x \Rightarrow \sin y = \frac{1}{x}\), aur \(y\) \(\sin^{-1}\) ki range mein hai: \(y = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\).

book_ref.quote: use a reciprocal identity, and read it back as an inverse function

blocks.prompt:
61 The relation \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) is true for:
(Rishta \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) kin \(x\) ke liye durust hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x < 0\) ho to \(\cot^{-1} x\) \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) mein hai magar \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) manfi; maslan \(\cot^{-1}(-1) = \frac{3\pi}{4}\).

book_ref.quote: Parts (i) and (ii) need no such restriction because the ranges already fit.

blocks.explanation: Har \(x \in [-1, 1]\) ke liye \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: each pair of 'co-functions' adds up to

blocks.prompt:
63 If \(\sec^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{5}\), then \(\csc^{-1} x\) equals:
(Agar \(\sec^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{5}\) ho to \(\csc^{-1} x\) kitna hai?)
